chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Aban, from Misma'a who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the instigation between the animals, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'I dislike that, except for the dogs.'

key_terms.أَكْرَهُ: I dislike (indicating karahah, a recommended dislike or non-forbidden status)
key_terms.الْبَهَائِمِ: Animals (specifically beasts of burden or livestock)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on instigating animals to fight?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between general animal cruelty and the specific utility of dogs, reflecting the Shia juristic principle of *istihsan* (juristic preference) where the exception is granted due to the dog's traditional role in hunting and guarding. This ruling highlights the nuanced approach of the Imams to *fiqh al-hayat* (jurisprudence of daily life), balancing ethical treatment of creation with practical human needs, a theme often discussed in later works like *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* and *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*.

en.hubeali: From him, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Aban, from Misma’a who said,
‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the instigation between the animals. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘I<sup>asws</sup> dislike that, except for the dogs’.
en.sarwar: 2. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Aban from Misma‘ who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about instigating animals against each other. He (the Imam) said, ‘I dislike it except dogs.’”
